newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces battle rebels in Algiers Casbah.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces battle rebels in Algiers Casbah.

text.p: Algerian security forces fought a seven-hour gunbattle with Moslem rebels on the heights of Algiers' ancient Casbah into the early hours of Thursday, residents said.
The clashes started on Wednesday at about 7.p.m. (1800 GMT) when security forces sealed off the High Casbah neighbourhood to eliminate some 12 guerrillas holed up there, residents said by telephone.
Crack troops arrived to reinforce the operation near the paramilitary gendarmerie headquarters three hours later.
"We then heard explosions, apparently grenades thrown by security forces into the gunmen's hideout," said one resident.
Sporadic firing continued until about 2.a.m. (0100 GMT) on Thursday, they said. Algerian authorities have not made any statement on the clashes.

Security forces have several times ringed and combed the Casbah and killed dozens of guerrillas in the winding streets of the old heart of the Algerian capital in the past three years. Very few prisoners have been taken, and security forces have used heavy weaponry to blast houses sheltering guerrillas.

The Casbah was a centre of Algerian resistance against French forces in Algeria's 1954-1962 war of independence, and French troops battled for months to try to end resistance there, never fully succeeding.
Residents said the guerrillas had built up their forces in the Casbah and made their presence known with the cold-blooded killing of more than 20 people there in the past four months.

Guerrillas from the Armed Islamic Group (GIA) recently posted leaflets on walls in the Casbah warning that they would kill women who still wore Western-style dress and banning men from smoking and reading newspapers.
The raid in the Casbah came less than two hours after President Liamine Zeroual reasserted that his government would fight and wipe out guerrillas.

"The Algerian nation is opposed firmly to terrorism carried out by criminals, traitors and mercenaries. The state is committed to fight terrorism with firmness," said Zeroual who was addressing a cabinet meeting on Wednesday.

They were the first remarks by Zeroual since the start of this year which has been marked by more rebel attacks against villages, and by bombings, mostly in Algiers and surrounding towns. More than 300 people have been killed since early November.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
